VAVEhub · valueengineeringhub.com · 15 October 2026

360° review of the site and both courses

I reviewed every page, both courses, the capstone, the toolkit, the exam and the account system after batches 1–5. Five separate audits, then fixes, then a re-test. Nothing below is live yet: it's waiting for your "Go".

VerdictScoresWhat I fixedBefore / afterContentNeeds youNext proposalsTests

Has it improved, and is it world-class yet?

Yes, it has improved a lot, and the learning content is now close to the best free courses. Batches 1–5 added what most course sites lack: labs you work through, worked examples that fade into practice, a spaced review, a capstone study, an exam marked on the server and a certificate anyone can check. Few paid courses have all of that.

It isn't world-class SaaS yet, mainly in look and flow, not in substance. The site still reads as a stylish personal site with two courses attached: five different page headers, decorative effects from an older design style (custom cursor, film grain, tilt cards), emoji used as icons, no "learner home" for people coming back, and no simple way to jump between modules on a phone.

The review also found real bugs that could lose a learner's work, two of them serious: opening the capstone on a second device wiped the saved study, and an older device could overwrite progress in the account. Those, and 50+ other bugs and errors, are fixed below and covered by new automatic tests.

What I fixed

Grouped by what a learner would notice. Each one was reproduced first, then fixed, then checked by a test.

SeverityProblem foundWhat happens now
CriticalOpening the capstone on a second device wiped the study saved to the account.The page reads the account copy first and uploads only newer work. If the account can't be reached, nothing is uploaded and the page says so.
CriticalAn older phone or laptop could overwrite Academy progress in the account (lost modules).Progress is read and merged before anything is uploaded; a failed read uploads nothing. Same for VAVE for Leaders.
BugA pass was lost if the learner reloaded before typing their name.The pass is kept for 30 days; the name box comes back after a reload.
BugLeaving the exam part-way (a reload or a sidebar click) threw the answers away.The paper and answers carry on after a reload; the browser asks before closing; visiting a module and coming back keeps the paper.
BugIf the reply was lost after marking, "Send my answers again" failed for ever.Sending the same paper twice returns the first result.
BugSeveral papers could be opened at once to dodge the one-hour wait after a fail.Only the newest paper can be marked, and only within three hours (database update).
BugRe-running the setup file let learners write their own certificates.Only the exam service can create a certificate, even if the setup file is run again (database update).
BugAn edited share link still showed "Verified" with the edited score.The certificate page shows the score and date on record.
BugCertificate dates showed a day early in the Americas.Dates are read as calendar dates in every time zone.
BugOn a shared computer, the next person inherited the last person's modules and certificate.Progress belongs to whoever signed in; a different person starts clean.
BugOn a phone, tapping a locked module seemed to do nothing.The course list folds away and the sign-in box comes into view with focus.
BugCapstone phases 4 and 6 were cut off on a phone.Their tables scroll sideways inside their own box.
BugPrinting any lesson gave blank pages.A lesson prints as itself; only an on-screen certificate prints on its own.
BugA saved candidate name in the Leaders pilot picker could run code.Saved names are shown as plain text and saved values are checked.
BugAsking for a sign-in code for an unknown email said "sign-ups are closed"; "Forgot password" could create an account.It says no account was found; only the sign-up form creates accounts.
BugIf the database was slow or down, signed-in learners were locked out.Signed-in learners keep access; the session is read from the browser.
BugThe practice dialog trapped no focus and leaked a key listener.Focus moves in, stays inside, and returns to the button on close.
Important17 private exam questions were readable in the public history.All 18 affected questions rewritten in the private bank (database update).
ImportantReloading after moving between modules reopened an old module.The address follows the module you choose.
ImportantFocus was lost after "Mark complete" and on the FAST board.Focus goes to the new module heading or board title.
ImportantAt 200% zoom the course header overflowed.Secondary links drop out at narrow widths; long buttons wrap.
ImportantSign-in errors weren't announced; the show-password label never changed.Errors are linked to their fields, the first one gets focus, the toggle says Show or Hide.
ImportantFlashcards and glossary terms hid their text from screen readers.Cards read the visible face; terms read their definition.
ImportantAfter each release, returning visitors ran old scripts with new pages.Scripts and styles always come fresh from the network first.
ImportantCertificate seals were 290 KB and 190 KB, downloaded on every course visit.25 KB each, and loaded only when shown; certificate fonts download once.
ImportantCapstone layout jumped as it loaded (shift 0.12 desktop, 0.18 phone).Shift is now 0 on both.
ImportantThe owner dashboard could be crashed or fooled by learner-edited data.Every field is checked; a pass counts when a certificate exists.
ImportantLeaders course page could be framed by another site.It now has the same framing guard as the other pages.
LayoutButtons had a grey bevel border; long labels ran off phones; the wordmark read "VAVE hub".Clean buttons, wrapping labels, and "VAVEhub" everywhere.
LayoutQuick-check answers were pills, so the long right answer stood out by shape.Full-width rows, and the right answer is no longer the longest.
LayoutCapstone: white checkboxes in dark mode, no arrow on "worked answer", last step cut off.Theme-coloured controls, an arrow that turns, all seven steps visible.
LayoutToolkit card buttons sat at different heights; formulas ran off the cheat sheet.Buttons line up at the bottom; formulas wrap; printable templates use the site font.
LayoutSmaller fixesTap targets 44 px on phones, closed menu links out of the Tab order, scroll-spy no longer sticks, cursor ring hidden until the mouse moves, content visible if scripts fail, YouTube thumbnail fallback, calendar file line folding, review keeps a module's stage when its question is missed.

Content accuracy and writing

Three content audits checked every module, guide, quiz, lab, template and the capstone against sources and against each other. Two helpers then made the corrections, and a third rewrote the quiz questions.

WhereErrorsWeaker claimsExamples of what changed
Academy, Modules 1–71147"Ten" creative approaches is now six; the 6-3-5 rhythm and sorting times are correct; payback sums separate annual saving from one-time cost; FMEA mentions the newer Action Priority method.
Academy, Modules 8–13, capstone, toolkit924Plant-utilisation overhead is about 1.5×, not 2×; the capstone sensitivity note is correct; the Nano dates are right; the healthy-programme figure is 68% in the module and the charter.
VAVE for Leaders, guides, legal pages920One wording for the 70–80% rule everywhere; the governance funnel adds up; the ideation simulator is a value ratio, not the Value Index; Terms cover both certificates.

Quizzes and challenges

In 88 of the 120 Academy quiz and challenge questions the right answer was the longest option, so a learner could often guess it. Now that's true of 13 questions (11%), and it is never a full clause longer than the others. Silly distractors such as "A coin flip" and "Use a bigger whiteboard" are replaced with mistakes people really make. Questions with two defensible answers were rewritten. The common-mistake hints were rebuilt to match.

Writing

The Leaders course was already the best-written part. Elsewhere, hype lines, hedges and stray em dashes were trimmed, and "certified course" wording now reads "course with a certificate" outside the certificate itself. The certificate wording is unchanged, as you asked.

1 · Database Run one SQL file in Supabase

It adds safe re-marking, the newest-paper rule, the certificate lock-down and the rewritten exam questions. Run it once, after I publish: Supabase → SQL Editor → New query → paste → Run. 2 · Narration New audio for changed modules

The narrated text changed in 13 Academy modules (m1–m13) and six Leaders modules (l0–l4, l6). After "Go" I'll start the narration workflow on GitHub for those modules; it takes about 30 minutes and needs nothing from you.

3 · Decisions Four questions only you can answer

  • Who issues the "PVA" and "TRIZ Certified" credentials named in the About section? Without a named issuer I'd suggest removing them.
  • Is the homepage YouTube video your own? If so, I'll credit it; if not, I'll name its owner.
  • Which email service sends the sign-in codes? The privacy policy should name it.
  • The certificate says "Value Engineering 360° Practitioner Course" and "certification examination". You asked me not to change it, so it stays. If you want it to match the rest of the site ("VE Academy", "final exam"), say so.

Tests

631 checks pass and 22 fail. The failures are the narration checks, which compare the page text with the recorded audio; they pass once the new narration is generated.

Two new test suites run on every push. Sync fakes the account database and plays two devices against each other: a second device opening the capstone, an older device opening the Academy, a slow or failed account read, a lost exam reply, an unknown email, and an edited certificate link. Robust covers exam resume, bad saved data, shared computers, deep links, dialog focus, escaping, time zones, printing and the small layout rules.
